## II. Independent Opinions of the Board of Supervisors

During the reporting period, in accordance with relative of Company Law, Articles of Association and rules of procedure of the BOS, the BOS conducted supervision and inspection diligently on statutory operation, financial position, related−party transactions and so on, which resulted in following independent opinion.

#### 锦州银行 Annual Report 2010 年度报告

### 1. Compliance with Relevant Laws and Regulations

In 2010, the Board of Supervisors attended all previous meetings of the Board of Directors and the Shareholders' General Meetings, and conducted strict supervision on decision-making procedure and performance of directors and senior executives.

The BOS considered the management team and the BOD was capable of standardized operating in accordance with Company Law and Articles of Association, making decisions scientifically and legally so as to gradually improve corporate governance structure, establish a relatively sound internal control mechanism, and form a standard management system. The directors and senior executives acted honestly, diligently and conscientiously, centered on the interests of the Bank in performing their duty, and strictly implemented all the resolutions and authorizations of the Shareholders' General Meetings so as to fulfill various operational plans and make good achievements. The information disclosure was timely and accurate. In fulfilling their duties, the directors and senior executives acted against no laws and regulations as well as Articles of Association. No infringement of the interests of investors was found.

### 2. The inspection of finance

During the reporting period, the BOS conducted supervision, examination and verification diligently and carefully on financial position and financial management. The BOS considered the Bank kept sound financial system, standardized financial operation, and fine financial position. Yuehua Certified Accountants Office conducted the auditing on 2010 financial statement and issued unqualified reports which reflected financial position and operational result truthfully, accurately, completely and impartially.

### 3. Auditing of the raised equity fund

As of Dec. 31, 2010, the registered capital of the Bank in 2009 reached 3.77223 billion Yuan, with infused additional registered capital of 1.225 billion Yuan. Yuehua Certified Accountants Office verified the previous paid-in of the newly-added equity and issued a Capital Verification Report accordingly.

The BOS considered, during the reporting period, the Bank used and managed collecting fund in accordance with administrative measure on collecting fund against no regulations and relevant rules by China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) in conformity with the development strategy of the Bank, by which the Bank promoted core competitiveness and overall profitability capacity. Related—party transactions were conducted openly, impartially and rationally in accord with the interest of all shareholders. No infringement of the interests of minority shareholders was found.

### 4. Acquisition and Disposal of Assets

During the reporting period, The BOS conducted supervision on acquisition, disposal of assets as well as decision-making and implementation of transactions. The BOS considered the transactions in accordance with laws, regulations and policies, on the principle of impartiality, openness and fairness in accord with the interest of the Bank and all the shareholders. No insider trading and infringement of the interest of shareholders were found.

### 5. Independent opinions on the related—party transactions

The related–party transactions during the reporting period were conducted as normal business and its price was determined by market prices based on the principle of fairness, impartiality and rationality in conformity with actual operation of the Bank. No insider trading and infringement of the interest of shareholders were found.

### 6. Internal Control System

During the reporting period, in order to establish sound internal control, prevent financial risks and guarantee the secured and stable operation of internal system, the Bank established complete, robust and effective internal control system to improve risk management capacity and guarantee the fulfillment of development strategy and operational target.

## Section X Major Events

## I. Major Litigation and Arbitration Cases

During the reporting period, no major litigation and arbitration cases occurred in the Bank.

## II. Acquisition and Disposal of Assets and Mergers and Acquisitions (“M&As”)

In accordance with the reply to the Establishment of Taihe Yimin Rural Bank of Jinzhou Corp., Ltd. [Jin Yinjian Fa (2010) No.27] issued by Jinzhou branch of the CBRC, on Jan 28, 2010, Taihe Yimin Rural Bank was officially opened

In accordance with the reply to the Establishment of Yi County Xianghe Rural Bank of Liaoning Corp., Ltd. [Jin Yinjian Fa (2010) No.346] issued by Jinzhou branch of the CBRC, on Nov 26, 2010, Yi County Xianghe Rural Bank was officially opened.

## III. Major related—party transactions for related corporate shareholders that hold 5% and above

The related–party transactions between the Bank and related parties are mainly concerning bank deposits and loans. All related–party transactions are necessary to the normal business activities. The Bank conducted its operations strictly in accordance with relevant laws and regulations as well as various business and management rules of the Bank when dealing with related–party transactions. The price is fairly set and the requirement is not lower than similar non–related transactions. There was no negative impact on the business performance and financial position of the Bank.

During the reporting period, the related corporate shareholders that hold 5% and above included Jinzhou Finance Bureau and Shenyang Guanyi Real Estate Co., Ltd. No major related-party transactions occurred.

# Report of the Auditors

ZR YH Shen Zi [2011] NO. 00223

To the shareholders of Bank of Jinzhou Co. Ltd.:

We have audited the accompanying financial statements of Bank of Jinzhou Co. Ltd. (the "Bank"), which comprise the balance sheet as at December 31, 2010, the income statement, the statement of equity changes and statement of cash flows for the year then ended and notes to these financial statements.

I. Management’s Responsibility for the Financial Statements

Management is responsible for the preparation of these financial statements in accordance with the Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises. This responsibility includes: designing, implementing and maintaining internal control relevant to the preparation of financial statements that are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error; selecting and applying appropriate accounting policies; and making accounting estimates that are reasonable in the circumstances.

## II. Auditor's Responsibility

Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial statements based on our audit. We conducted our audit in accordance with the China Auditing Standards. Those standards require that we comply with ethical requirements and plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance whether the financial statements are free from material misstatement.

An audit involves performing procedures to obtain audit evidence about the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. The procedures selected depend on the auditor's judgment, including the assessment of the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to fraud or error. In making those risk assessments, the auditor considers internal control relevant to the entity's preparation of the financial statements in order to design audit procedures that are appropriate in the circumstances, but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the entity's internal control. An audit also includes evaluating the appropriateness of accounting policies used and the reasonableness of accounting estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the financial statements.

We believe that the audit evidence we have obtained is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our audit opinion.

#### Ⅲ.0pinion

In our opinion, the financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Bank as of December 31, 2010, and of its financial performance and its cash flows for the year then ended in accordance with the Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises.

# Bank of Jinzhou Co., Ltd. Notes to Financial Statements

December 31, 2010

(Unless otherwise specified, RMB Yuan is used as the unit of the amount of money)

## I. General Situations

Bank of Jinzhou Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "the Bank" for short) is a joint-equity corporation co-sponsored and established by 14 legal entities which consist of 16 Urban Credit Cooperatives including Lingyun Urban Credit Cooperatives, Jinzhou Financial Bureau, Jinzhou Petrochemical Tianyan Group Co., Ltd as well as Jinzhou Department Store with approval of the People's Bank of China on the Written Reply to the Establishment of Jinzhou Urban Cooperative Bank [Yin Fu (1997) No.29] in accordance with the spirit of the Notice Regarding the Establishment of Urban Cooperative Banks[Guo Fu (1995) No.25] issued by the State Council. The original name of the Bank is Jinzhou City Urban Cooperative Bank and was renamed as Jinzhou City Commercial Bank Co., Ltd on April 12, 2008 pursuant to the document Notice of Some Problems on Changing the Name of Urban Cooperative Banks [Yin Fu (1998) No.94], jointly issued by the People's Bank of China and State Industrial and Commercial Administrations, and was renamed as Bank of Jinzhou Co., Ltd on April 14, 2008, with approval of China Banking Regulatory Commission on the written Reply of China Banking Regulatory Commission about Renaming Jinzhou City Commercial Bank[Yin Jian Fu (2008) No.137].

The Business License Serial Number of the Bank is 210700004032898; the Finance License Code is B0127H2210001; the registered capital is 3.7722339 billion RMB Yuan; legal representative is Zhang Wei; and registered address is 69 Shifu Road, Taihe District, Jinzhou. By the end of reporting date, the biggest shareholder of the Bank was Jinzhou Financial Bureau with a shareholding proportion of 6.31%.

In accordance with the reply to the Establishment of Taihe Yimin Rural Bank of Jinzhou Corp., Ltd. [Jin Yinjian Fa (2010) No.27] issued by Jinzhou Branch of the CBRC, on Jan 28, 2010, Taihe Yimin Rural Bank was officially opened.

In accordance with the reply to the Establishment of Haerbin Branch of Bank of Jinzhou Co., Ltd. [Hei Yinjian Fu (2010) No.69] issued by Heilongjiang Branch of the CBRC, on Apr 12, 2010, Haerbin Branch of the Bank was officially opened.

In accordance with the reply to the Establishment of Dandong Branch of Bank of Jinzhou Co., Ltd. [Liao Yinjian Fu (2010) No.205] issued by Liaoning Branch of the CBRC, on July 10, 2010, Dandong Branch of the Bank was officially opened.

In accordance with the reply to the Establishment of Yi County Xianghe Rural Bank of Liaoning Corp., Ltd. [Jin Yinjian Fa (2010) No.346] issued by Jinzhou branch of the CBRC, on Nov 26, 2010, Yi County Xianghe Rural Bank was officially opened.

In accordance with the reply to the Establishment of Beijing Branch of Bank of Jinzhou Co., Ltd. [Yinjian Fu (2010) No.594] issued by the CBRC, Beijing Branch of the Bank was approved for the establishment.

Under the Bank, there are 2 holding companies, which consist of Taihe Yimin Rural Bank of Jinzhou Corp., Ltd and Yi County Xianghe Rural Bank of Liaoning Corp., Ltd, and there are 5 branches including Tianjin Branch, Shenyang Branch, Dalian Branch, Haerbin Branch and Dandong Branch. In addition, there are 129 sub-branches

for the entire Bank.

The business scope of the Bank covers the following: absorbing public deposits, granting short, medium and long-term loans, handling domestic and international settlement, handling bill acceptance and discount, acting as an agent to issue financial bonds, acting as an agent for issuing, honoring and underwriting of government bonds, buying and selling government bond and financial bond, engaging in inter-bank lending, trading foreign exchanges for the Bank or on behalf of its customers, engaging in bank card business, providing letter of credit and financial guarantees, acting as an agent to handle collection and payment of money and issuance business as well, offering safe box service, and other businesses approved by China Banking Regulatory Commission.

The financial report was approved for declaration by the Board of Directors on Mar 2, 2011.

## II. Statement on Abiding by Accounting Standard for Business Enterprises

The financial report prepared by the Bank is in accordance with the requirement of Accounting Standard for Business Enterprises, which genuinely and integrally reflects the financial position by Dec 31, 2010, business performance and cash flow for the year 2010 and other relevant information of the Bank.

#### Ⅲ. Basis of Preparation

The financial statements of the Bank was prepared with assumption of sustained operation, on the basis of transactions and matters which actually occurred, in accordance with Accounting Standard for Business Enterprises—Basic Criterion issued by the Ministry of Finance in February, 2006 and 38 concrete accounting standards, application guidelines, explanations, and other relevant rules issued later (thereafter referred to as Accounting Standard for Business Enterprises).

## IV. Important Accounting Policies and Accounting Estimates

1. Important Accounting Policies

1. Accounting year

The Bank's accounting year starts on January 1 and ends on December 31.

2. Recording currency

The recording currency of the Bank is RMB.

3. Accounting methods for business combination

The term "business combinations" refers to a transaction or event bringing together two or more separate enterprises into one reporting entity. Business combinations are classified into the business combinations under the same control and the business combinations not under the same control.

(1) Business combination under the same control

A business combination under the same control is a business combination in which all of the combining enterprises are ultimately controlled by the same party or the same parties both before and after the business combination and on which the control is not temporary. In a business combination under the same control, the party which obtains control of other combining enterprise(s) on the combining date is the combining party, the other combining enterprise(s) is (are) the combined party. The "combining date" refers to the date on which the combining party actually obtains control on the combined party

The assets and liabilities that the combining party obtains in a business combination shall be measured on the basis of their carrying amount in the combined party on the combining date. As for the balance between the carrying amount of the net assets obtained by the combining party and the carrying amount of the consideration paid by it (or the total par value of the shares issued), the additional paid-in capital shall be adjusted. If the

additional paid—in capital is not sufficient to be offset, the retained earnings shall be adjusted.

The direct cost for the business combination of the combining party shall be recorded into the profits and losses at the current period.

(2) Business combination not under the same control

A business combination not under the same control is a business combination in which the combining enterprises are not ultimately controlled by the same party or the same parties both before and after the business combination.

In a business combination not under the same control, the party which obtains the control on other combining enterprise(s) on the purchase date is the acquirer, and other combining enterprise(s) is (are) the acquired. The "acquisition date" refers to the date on which the acquirer actually obtains the control on the acquired.

For a business combination not under the same control, if the acquisition date is on or before Dec 31, 2009, the combination costs shall be the fair values, on the acquisition date, of the assets paid, the liabilities incurred or assumed and the equity securities issued by the acquirer in exchange for the control on the acquired. If the acquisition date is on or after Jan 1, 2010, the combination costs shall only be the fair values, on the acquisition date, of the assets paid, the liabilities incurred or assumed and the equity securities issued by the acquirer in exchange for the control on the acquired. The intermediary expenses including the expenses for audit, assessment and legal services and other management expenses for the business combination shall be recorded into the profits and losses at the current period.

The trading expenses of equity securities or debt securities issued for the business combination shall be recorded into the amount at their initial recognition. If the acquisition date is on or before Dec 31, 2009, where any future event that is likely to affect the combination costs is likely to occur and its effects on the combination costs can be measured reliably, the acquirer shall record the said contingent consideration into the combination costs. If the acquisition date is on or after Jan 1, 2010, the acquirer shall record the said contingent consideration into the cost of business combination according to fair value on the acquisition date. Where any new and further evidence on the existing situation occurs within 12 months after the acquisition date which makes the said contingent consideration adjusted, the combined business reputation shall be adjusted correspondingly.

For a business combination realized by two or more transactions of exchange, if the acquisition date is on or before Dec 31, 2009, the combination costs shall be the summation of the costs of all separate transactions.

If the acquisition date is on or after Jan 1, 2010, in the consolidated financial statements of the Bank, the equity held by the acquirer on the acquired before the acquisition date, shall make another measurement according to its fair value on the acquisition date, the gap between the carrying amount and the fair value shall be computed into the current investment income. Meanwhile, other comprehensive income related to the equity held by the acquirer on the acquired before the acquisition date shall be transferred into the current investment income. The combination costs shall be the summation of the fair value of the equity on the acquisition date held on the acquired before the acquisition date and the fair value of the additional equity held on the acquired on the acquisition date.

The acquirer shall measure the combination costs and obtained identifiable net assets from the combination according to their fair value on the acquisition date. The acquirer shall recognize the positive balance between the combination costs and the fair value of the identifiable net assets it obtains from the acquired as business reputation. The acquirer shall treat the balance between the combination costs and the fair value of the identifiable net assets it obtains from the acquired as follows: first it shall reexamine the measurement of the fair values of the identifiable assets, liabilities and contingent liabilities it obtains from the acquired as well as the combination

costs; If, after the reexamination, the combination costs are still less than the fair value of the identifiable net assets it obtains from the acquired, it shall record the balance into the profits and losses of the current period.

Deductible temporary difference obtained by the acquirer on the acquired is not recognized failing to meet the requirement of deferred income tax on the acquisition date, but within 12 months after the acquisition date, where new or further information indicates that the relevant situation on the acquisition date has already existed and the economic interests of the deductible temporary difference by the acquired on the acquisition date are expected to realize, it shall be recognized as deferred income tax asset, and business reputation shall be deducted which, if insufficient to write down, the balance shall be recognized as current profit and loss. Except for the above-mentioned situation, the deferred income tax asset recognized related to business combination shall be recorded into current profit and loss.

### 4. Method for preparation of consolidated financial statements

##### (1) Recognition principle on the scope of consolidated financial statements

The scope of consolidated financial statements is recognized based on the control, which means the Bank is capable of financial and operational policy-decision on the invested enterprise, and accordingly have the right of obtaining the interest from the operation of the invested enterprise. The scope includes the Bank and all subsidiary companies which refer to enterprises and entities controlled by the Bank.

##### (2) Method for preparation of consolidated financial statements

Starting from the day of acquiring net asset of subsidiary company and actual control right of business decision, the Bank shall bring them into combination scope and stop doing so since the day of forfeiting the right. For disposed subsidiary, the operational results and cash flow before the handling day have been included in the consolidated profit statements and cash flow statements, and for currently disposal subsidiary, the beginning sum of the consolidated balance sheet shall not be adjusted. For the added subsidiary due to business combination not under the same control, because the operational results and cash flow before acquisition date have been included in the consolidated profit statements and cash flow statements, the beginning sum and comparison sum in the consolidated financial statements shall not be adjusted. For the added subsidiary due to business combination under the same control as well as the combined party under the acquisition, the operational results and cash flow from the beginning to the end of combination have been suitably included in the consolidated profit statements and cash flow statements, the comparison sum of consolidated financial statements.

In preparing consolidated financial statements, Where, during a business combination under the same control, the accounting policy adopted by the combined party is different from that adopted by the combining party, the combining party shall, according to accounting policy and accounting period it adopts, adjust the relevant items in the financial statements of the combined party. For the subsidiary acquired not under the same control, its financial statements shall be adjusted based on fair value of identifiable net assets on the acquisition date.

All major current balance, transaction and unrealized profit shall be eliminated in preparing financial statements.

Shareholders equity of the subsidiary and the parts in its net profit or loss not owned by the Bank appear respectively on the consolidated financial statements as the item of minority shareholders' equity and the item of shareholders' equity and net profit. The shares owned by minority shareholders in current net profit or loss of the subsidiary show under the item of net profit on the consolidated profit statements as minority shareholders' equity. Any excess of the loss of subsidiary shared by minority shareholders over the shares owned at the beginning of owner's equity, minority shareholders' equity is eliminated.

When the controlling right over original subsidiary is forfeited due to dealing with partial equity investment or other reason, if it is forfeited on or before Dec 31, 2009, with regard to the remaining equity, book value of long-term equity investments under cost method on the separate financial statements shall be regarded as initial investment cost; if it is forfeited on or after Jan 1, 2010, the remaining equity shall make another measurement at the fair value at the date of forfeiting controlling right.

The difference between the sum of the consideration acquired in dealing with equity and fair value of the remaining equity ( less net asset calculated continuously from purchasing date at original share proportion ) is charged to investment gains at current period of forfeiting controlling right.

Other comprehensive income in relation with the investment of original subsidiary is all transferred to current investment income. Thereafter, the remaining equity shall be subject to the follow-up measurement in accordance with the relevant rules in Accounting Standard for Business Enterprises No. 2-long-term equity investment and Accounting Standard for Business Enterprises No. 22 — Recognition and Measurement of Financial Instruments. For details, see IV.10 long-term equity investment and item IV7 financial assets in this Notes.

## 5. Measurement method for foreign currency transactions and the conversion of foreign currency financial statements

The Bank adopts separate accounting system for measurement in terms of different currencies involved in its operation, and prepare financial statements in RMB at the end of the term. While preparing conversion financial statements in RMB, the Bank shall first prepare financial statements in different currencies respectively, and then convert different currencies into RMB, under which it shall prepare its financial statements in BMB.

Foreign currency transaction shall be recorded at exchange rate of trading day, and gains or losses of exchange arising from foreign business as well as gains or losses of exchange arising from the conversion of monetary assets and liabilities into functional currency shall be calculated at exchange rate at trading day or balance sheet day. Income and expense items denominated in foreign currencies shall be converted at spot exchange rate of trading day and the gains or losses arising therefrom shall be recorded into the profit statement.

For non-monetary items, the conversion gap of transaction financial assets shall be recorded into profits and losses of fair value changes, and the conversion gap of available-for-sale investemnt shall be included in the reserve of fair value changes in owner's equity.

### 6. Cash and cash equivalents

Cash and cash equivalents refers to all cash in hand and call deposits in banks readily available for making payments, highly—liquid investments with a maturity of less than three months from the date of acquisition that are readily convertible to known amounts of cash and which are subject to an insignificant risk of change in value, Deposits with the PBOC (exclusive of legal reserve), Deposits in correspondent banks, Due to banks due from banks and capital lent, Assets purchased under resale agreements, etc.

7. Accounting method of financial assets and financial liabilities

(1) Determination method of the fair value of financial assets and financial liabilities

The "fair value" refers to the amount, at which both parties to a transaction who are familiar with the condition exchange their assets or clear off their debts under fair conditions. As for the financial instruments for which there is an active market, the quoted prices in the active market shall be used to determine the fair values thereof. The quoted prices in the active market refer to the prices, which are easily available from the stock exchanges, brokers, industry associations, pricing service institutions and etc. at a fixed term, and which represent the prices

at which actually occurred market transactions are made under fair conditions. Where there is no active market for a financial instrument, the enterprise concerned shall adopt value appraisal techniques to determine its fair value. The value appraisal techniques mainly include the prices adopted by the parties, who are familiar with the condition, in the latest market transaction upon their own free will, the current fair value obtained by referring to other financial instruments of the same essential nature, the cash flow capitalization method and the option pricing model, etc.

The sale of financial assets in conventional way shall conduct accounting confirmation and terminate confirmation as trading day. When they are initially recognized, financial assets are divided into financial assets which are measured at their fair value and of which the variation is recorded into the current profits and losses, held-to-maturity investment, loans and the account receivables, and available-for-sale financial assets. When they are initially recognized, financial assets are measured at their fair value. As for financial assets which are measured at their fair value and of which the variation is recorded into the current profits and losses, relevant transaction expenses are directly recorded into the current profits and losses, and as for other financial assets, relevant transaction expenses are recorded into initially-recognized amount.

①Financial assets which are measured at their fair value and of which the variation is recorded into the current profits and losses.

Those assets include transactional financial assets and the designated financial assets which are measured at their fair value and of which the variation is recorded into the current profits and losses. The group's financial assets which are measured at their fair value and of which the variation is recorded into the current profits and losses are all called transactional financial assets.

The financial assets meeting any of the following requirements shall be classified as transactional financial assets: (1) the purpose to acquire the said financial assets is mainly for selling or repurchase of them in the near future; (2) forming a part of the identifiable combination of financial instruments which are managed in a centralized way and for which there are objective evidences proving that the enterprise may manage the combination by way of short-term profit making in the near future; (3) being a derivative instrument, excluding the designated derivative instruments which are effective hedging instruments, or derivative instruments to financial guarantee contracts, and the derivative instruments which are connected with the equity instrument investments for which there is no quoted price in the active market, whose fair value cannot be reliably measured, and which shall be settled by delivering the said equity instruments.

Transactional financial assets shall make subsequent measurement according to their fair value. The profits and losses that arise when fair value changes as well as dividend and interest income relate to the said financial assets shall be recorded into the current profits and losses.

The term “held-to-maturity” refers to a non-derivative financial asset with a fixed date of maturity, a fixed or determinable amount of repo price and which the enterprise holds for a definite purpose or the enterprise is able to hold until its maturity.

Held—to—maturity investment shall make subsequent measurement on the basis of the post—amortization costs by adopting the actual interest rate method. The profits and losses that arise when such financial assets are terminated from recognition, or are impaired of amortized, shall be recorded into the profits and losses of the current period.

The actual interest rate method refers to the method by which the post-amortization costs and the interest incomes of different installments or interest expenses are calculated in light of the actual interest rates of the financial assets or financial liabilities (including a set of financial assets or financial liabilities). The actual interest rate refers to the interest rate adopted to cash the future cash flow of a financial asset or financial liability within the predicted term of existence or within a shorter applicable term into the current carrying amount of the financial asset or financial liability.

When the actual interest rate is calculated, the future cash flow shall be predicted on the basis of taking into account all the contractual provisions concerning the financial asset or financial liability (the future credit losses shall not be taken into account). Meanwhile, the various fee charges, trading expenses, premiums or reduced values, etc., which are paid or collected by the parties to a financial asset or financial liability contract and which form a part of the actual interests rate, shall also be taken into consideration.

Where the intention of holding or the ability to hold changes, if a certain investment is no longer classified as held-to-maturity investment, it shall be re-classified as sellable financial asset, which shall make subsequent measurement at its fair value. If the amount sold or re-classified in the held-to-maturity investment is considerably larger, which is exclusive of Article 16 of Accounting Standard for Business Enterprises No. 22 — Recognition and Measurement of Financial Instruments, which makes the surplus of such investment unsuited to be classified as held-to-maturity investment, the surplus of such investment shall be re-classified as a sellable financial asset which shall make subsequent measurement at its fair value. After the re-classification, such financial assets shall not be classified as a held-to-maturity investment within the current accounting year and the following two complete accounting years. The gap between the carrying amount of the said remnant part of the investment at the re-classification day and the fair value shall be computed into the owner's equity. And when the said sellable financial asset is impaired or transferred out when it is terminated from recognition, it shall be recorded into the profits and losses of the current period.

### ③ Loans and accounts receivable

Loans and accounts receivable refers to the non-derivative financial assets for which there is no quoted price in the active market and of which the repo amount is fixed or determinable, including customers' loans and investment in voucher-based national debt.

Loans and accounts receivable shall make subsequent measurement on the basis of the post-amortization costs by adopting the actual interest rate method. The profits and losses that arise when such financial assets are terminated from recognition, or are impaired of amortized, shall be recorded into the profits and losses of the current period.

④ sellable financial assets

The sellable financial assets include the non-derivative financial assets which are designated as sellable when they are initially recognized as well as the financial assets other than financial assets measured at their fair values and of which the variation is recorded into the profits and losses of the current period, loans and accounts receivables, and investments held until their maturity.

The sellable financial assets shall make subsequent measurement at their fair value. The profits and losses arising from the change in the fair value shall be recognized as other comprehensive income and included in capital reserve with the exception of impairment losses and the gap arising from foreign exchange convention of cash financial assets in any foreign currency and post-amortization cost, and when the said financial asset is stopped from recognition and is transferred out, it shall be recorded into the profits and losses of the current period.

It shall be accounted for as current profit or loss when the financial assets stop recognition to be transferred.

The interest acquired during the period of holding the sellable financial assets and cash dividend for which the invested announces to distribute shall be recorded into investment income.

Where the intention of holding or the ability to hold changes, or the fair value can not be reliably measured any more, or the term of holding has exceeded “two complete accounting years” as described in Article 16 of Accounting Standard for Business Enterprises No. 22 — Recognition and Measurement of Financial Instruments, which makes it no longer suitable to measure the financial asset or financial liability at its fair value, the enterprise concerned may measure the said financial asset or financial liability on the basis of its cost or post-amortization cost. And such cost or post-amortization cost at the re-classification day shall be the fair value or carrying amount of the financial asset or financial liability.

Where such financial asset has a fixed date of maturity, the gains or losses that are related to the said financial asset and that are directly included in other comprehensive income, shall be amortized within the remaining period of the said financial asset by adopting the actual interest rate method and be recorded into the profits and losses of the current period. The gap between the post-amortization cost of the financial asset and the amount on the maturity date shall also be amortized within the remaining period of the said financial asset by adopting the actual interest rate method and be recorded into the profits and losses of the current period. Where such financial asset does not have a fixed date of maturity, the gains or losses that are included in other comprehensive income shall remain in the owner's equity. And when the said financial asset is transferred out at its disposal, it shall be recorded into the profits and losses of the current period.

## (3). Impairment of financial assets

the Bank shall carry out an inspection, on each balance sheet day, on the carrying amount of other financial assets other than hose measured at their fair values and of which the variation is recorded into the profits and losses of the current period. Where there is any objective evidence proving that such financial asset has been impaired, an impairment provision shall be made.

An impairment test shall be made on the financial assets with significant single amounts. With regard to the financial assets with insignificant single amounts, an independent impairment test may be carried out, or they may be included in a combination of financial assets with similar credit risk features so as to carry out an impairment-related test. Where, upon independent test, the financial asset (including those financial assets with significant single amounts and those with insignificant amounts) has not been impaired, it shall be included in a combination of financial assets with similar risk so as to conduct another impairment test. The financial assets which have suffered from an impairment loss in any single amount shall not be included in any combination of financial assets with similar risk features for any impairment test.

①impairment of Held—to—maturity investment, Loans and accounts receivable

Where a financial asset measured on the basis of the costs or post-amortization costs is impaired, the carrying amount of the said financial asset shall be written down to the current value of the predicted future cash flow, and the amount as written down shall be recognized as loss of the impairment of the asset and shall be recorded into the profits and losses of the current period. Where the said financial asset is recognized as having suffered from any impairment loss, if there is any objective evidence proving that the value of the said financial asset has been restored, and it is objectively related to the events that occur after such loss is recognized, the impairment-related losses as originally recognized shall be reversed. However, the reversed carrying amount shall

not be any more than the post—amortization costs of the said financial asset on the day of reverse under the assumption that no provision is made for the impairment.

②impairment of sellable financial assets

Where a sellable financial asset is impaired, the accumulative losses arising from the decrease of the fair value of the capital reserve which was directly included shall be transferred out and recorded into the profits and losses of the current period. The accumulative losses that are transferred out shall be the balance obtained from the initially obtained costs of the sold financial asset after deducting the principals as taken back, the current fair value and the impairment-related losses as was recorded into the profits and losses of the current period.

Where the said financial asset is recognized as having suffered from any impairment loss, if there is any objective evidence proving that the value of the said financial asset has been restored, and it is objectively related to the events that occur after such loss is recognized, the impairment—related losses as originally recognized shall be reversed. The impairment loss of the Sellable equity instrument investment shall be reversed and recognized as other comprehensive income, and the impairment loss of the sellable debt instrument shall be reversed and recorded into the profits and losses of the current period.

However, the impairment—related losses incurred to an equity instrument investment for which there is no quoted price in the active market and whose fair value cannot be reliably measured, or incurred to a derivative financial asset which is connected with the said equity instrument and which shall be settled by delivering the said equity instrument, may not be reversed.

(4) Recognition basis and measurement method of the transfer of financial assets

Where a financial asset satisfies any of the following requirement, the recognition shall be terminated: ① where the contractual rights for collecting the cash flow of the said financial asset are terminated; ② where the said financial asset has been transferred and nearly all of the risks and rewards related to the ownership of the financial asset has been transferred to the transferee; ③ Where an enterprise does not transfer or retain nearly all of the risks and rewards related to the ownership of a financial asset, but it gives up its control over the financial asset.

Where an enterprise does not transfer or retain nearly all of the risks and rewards related to the ownership of a financial asset, and it doesn't give up its control over the financial asset, it shall, according to the extent of its continuous involvement in the transferred financial asset, recognize the related financial asset and recognize the relevant liability accordingly. The term "continuous involvement in the transferred financial asset" shall refer to the risk level that the enterprise faces resulting from the change of the value of the financial asset.

If the transfer of an entire financial asset satisfies the conditions for stopping recognition, the difference between the amounts of the book value of the transferred financial asset and the sum of consideration received from the transfer, and the accumulative amount of the changes of the fair value originally recorded in the owner's equities (in the event that the financial asset involved in the transfer is a financial asset available for sale), shall be recorded in the profits and losses of the current period.

If the transfer of partial financial asset satisfies the conditions to stop the recognition, the entire book value of the transferred financial asset shall, between the portion whose recognition has been stopped and the portion whose recognition has not been stopped, be apportioned according to their respective relative fair value, and the difference between the amounts of the sum of the consideration obtained for the transfer and the accumulative amount of the changes in the fair value originally recorded in the comprehensive income which shall be amortized

to the portion whose recognition has been stopped, and amortized above—mentioned carrying amounts shall be included into the profits and losses of the current period.

(5) The classification and measurement of financial liabilities.

When they are initially recognized, financial liabilities are divided into financial liabilities which are measured at their fair value and of which the variation is recorded into the current profits and losses and other financial liabilities. As for financial liabilities which are measured at their fair value and of which the variation is recorded into the current profits and losses, relevant transaction expenses are directly recorded into the current profits and losses, and as for other financial liabilities, relevant transaction expenses are recorded into initially—recognized amount.

① financial liabilities which are measured at their fair value and of which the variation is recorded into the current profits and losses

Those liabilities include transactional financial liabilities and the designated financial liabilities which are measured at their fair value and of which the variation is recorded into the current profits and losses on the initial recognition, which is the same as the financial assets classified into transactional financial assets and the designated financial assets which are measured at their fair value and of which the variation is recorded into the current profits and losses on the initial recognition.

The financial liabilities which are measured at their fair value and of which the variation is recorded into the current profits and losses shall make subsequent measurement according to their fair value. The profits and losses that arise when fair value changes as well as dividend and interest income relate to the said financial liabilities shall be recorded into the current profits and losses.

② other financial liabilities

The financial liabilities connected with the equity instrument investments for which there is no quoted price in the active market, whose fair value cannot be reliably measured, and which shall be settled by delivering the said equity instruments shall make consequent measurement at their costs. Other financial liabilities shall make subsequent measurement on the basis of the post—amortization costs by adopting the actual interest rate method. The profits and losses that arise when such financial assets are terminated from recognition, or are impaired of amortized, shall be recorded into the profits and losses of the current period.

③ financial guarantee contracts and loan commitments

the financial guarantee contracts which are exclusive of the financial liabilities which are measured at their fair value and of which the variation is recorded into the current profits and losses, or the loan commitments under the market interest rate which are not designated as financial liabilities which are measured at their fair value and of which the variation is recorded into the current profits and losses shall be measured at their fair value on the initial recognition. After the initial recognition, they will make subsequent measurement according to the larger amount of the balance of the amount recognized in accordance with Accounting Standard for Business Enterprises No. 13—Contingencies and the amount on the initial recognition (less the accumulated amortized amount recognized in accordance with Accounting Standard for Business Enterprises No. 13—Incomes).

(6) The termination of recognition of financial liabilities

Only when the prevailing obligations of a financial liability are relieved in all or in part may the recognition of the financial liability be terminated in all or partly. Where the Bank enters into an agreement with a creditor, so as to substitute the existing financial liabilities by way of any new financial liability, and if the contractual

stipulations regarding the new financial liability is substantially different from that regarding the existing financial liability, it shall terminate the recognition of the existing financial liability, and shall at the same time recognize the new financial liability.

Where the recognition of a financial liability is totally or partially terminated, the enterprise concerned shall include into the profits and losses of the current period the gap between the carrying amount which has been terminated from recognition and the considerations it has paid (including the non-cash assets it has transferred out and the new financial liabilities it has assumed).

## (7) The reinsurance of financial assets and financial liabilities

When the Bank has the legal right of offsetting the recognized financial assets and financial liabilities, which is executable at present, in the same time the Bank plan to settle it in net amount, or cash the said financial assets and pay the said financial liabilities, the balance of the reinsurance of financial assets and financial liabilities shall be shown separately on the balance sheet. Apart from the above-mentioned situation, financial assets and financial liabilities shall be shown separately on the balance sheet against reinsurance.

### 8. Amount purchased under resale agreements and amount sold under repurchase agreements

The term “purchased under resale agreements” means a contract that the Bank buys in relevant assets from its trading opponent at a certain price according to stipulations in contract or agreement (including bonds, bills and loans), and then resells to the opposite side at the specified price at the date specified under contract. Amount purchased under resale agreements is to be charged to account according to actual payment as the relevant assets are bought in.

The term “sold under repurchase agreements” refers to a contract that the Bank sells relevant assets (including bonds, sold bills) to its trading opponent at a certain price according to stipulations under contract or agreement, and then buys back from the opposite side at a specified price at the date specified under contract. Amount sold under repurchase agreements is charged to account according to amount actually received as the relevant assets are sold out.

The bid—ask spread between amount purchased under resale agreements and amount sold under repurchase agreements shall be recognized as interest income or expense at actual interest rate method during the periods.

### 9. Derivative financial instruments

Derivative financial instruments refer to derivative financial products established on the basis of basic products or basic underlying variables with its price being decided upon the change of later. Financial instruments include forward contract, futures contract, interchange and future right, as well as implements with one or more their characteristics. Initial measurement shall be confirmed on the basis of fair value on the day when the derivative trading contract is reached and be subsequently measured based on fair value. Value of assessment earnings or assessment deficit produced due to the changes in fair value are charged to current gains and losses, and simultaneously reflected in “derivative financial assets” or “derivative financial liabilities” items of the statement of assets and liabilities.

Some derivative financial instruments are embedded in non-derivative financial instruments (i.e. principal contract). The embedded derivative financial instruments and principal contract compose a hybrid instrument. If the hybrid instrument related with embedded derivative instruments has not been appointed as financial assets or liabilities which are measured based on fair value and their changes are charged to current gains and losses, and the following conditions are satisfied at the same time, this embedded derivative instruments should be split off.

the hybrid instrument and treated as individual measurement derivative instruments.

① No close relation with the principal contract exists in terms of economic futures and risks

② Having the same conditions as embedded derivative instruments. The instruments solely existed are also derivative financial instruments.

10. Long-term Equity Investments

(1) the recognition of investment costs

As for the long-term equity investment formed in the business combination, if the business combination is under the same control, it shall on the acquisition date, regard the share of the book value of the owner's equity of the acquired enterprise as the initial cost of the long-term equity investment.

For the business combination not under the same control, if the acquisition date is on or before Dec 31, 2009, the acquirer shall regard the combination costs as the initial cost of the long-term equity investment. If the acquisition date is on or after Jan 31, 2010, the combination costs shall be the sum of fair value of the assets paid, the liabilities incurred or assumed and the equity securities issued. The intermediary expenses including the expenses for audit, assessment and legal services and other management expenses for the business combination shall be recorded into the profits and losses at the current period. The trading expenses of equity securities or debt securities issued for the business combination shall be recorded into the amount at their initial recognition.

Besides the long-term equity investments formed by the merger of enterprises, other equity investments shall make initial measurement at their costs, which shall be recognized according to purchase cost in cash which is actually paid, the fair value of equity securities issued by the Bank, the value stipulated in the investment contract or agreement, the fair value or original carrying amount of transferred assets by the exchange of non-monetary assets, the fair value of the said fair value. The expenses directly relevant to the obtainment of the long-term equity investment, taxes and other necessary expenses are also recorded into the investment costs.

(2) Subsequent Measurement and recognition measure of profits and losses

A long-term equity investment of the investing enterprise that does not do joint control or does not have significant influences on the invested entity, and has no offer in the active market and its fair value cannot be reliably measured, shall be measured by adopting the cost method; A long-term equity investment that do joint control or has significant influences on the invested entity shall be measured by adopting the equity method; A long-term equity investment of the investing enterprise that does not do control or does not have significant influences on the invested entity, and its fair value can be reliably measured, shall be measured by adopting the sellable financial assets method;

In addition, the financial statements of the Bank make the measurement on the long-term equity investment which do control on the invested entity by adopting the cost method.

①the long-term equity investment measured by employing the cost method

By employing the cost method, the long-term equity investment shall be included at its initial investment cost. The current income shall be recognized according to the dividends in cash or profits declared to distribute by the invested entity with the exception of the actually-paid amount or the dividends in cash or profits included in the consideration which have been declared to distribute.

②the long-term equity investment measured by employing the equity method

By employing the equity method, if the initial cost of a long-term equity investment is more than the investing enterprise's attributable share of the fair value of the invested entity's identifiable net assets for the investment,

the initial cost of the long-term equity investment may not be adjusted. If the initial cost of a long-term equity investment is less than the investing enterprise' attributable share of the fair value of the invested entity's identifiable net assets for the investment, the difference shall be included in the current profits and losses and the cost of the long-term equity investment shall be adjusted simultaneously.

by employing the equity method, the profits and losses of the current investment shall be the attributable share of the net profits or losses of the invested entity. The investing enterprise shall, on the ground of the fair value of all identifiable assets of the invested entity when it obtains the investment, and in accordance with the Bank's accounting policies and accounting period, recognize the attributable share of the net profits and losses of the invested entity after it adjusts the net profits of the invested entity.

For the unrealized profits and losses of internal transaction incurred between the Bank and its joint enterprise and associated entity, the part owned by the Bank calculated according to the proportion of shares shall be set off and on this basis investment profits and losses shall be recognized. But For the unrealized profits and losses of internal transaction incurred between the Bank and its invested entity, the transferred asset impairment in accordance with the Accounting Standards for Enterprises No. 8 — Asset Impairment shall not be set off.

For the other comprehensive income of the invested entity, the book value of the long-term equity investment shall be adjusted accordingly and recognized as other comprehensive income and recorded into Additional paid-in capital.

An investing enterprise shall recognize the net losses of the invested enterprise until the book value of the long-term equity investment and other long-term rights and interests which substantially form the net investment made to the invested entity are reduced to zero. In addition, if the investing enterprise has the obligation to undertake extra losses, it shall recognize predicted liabilities in the light of predicted assumed obligation and recorded it into the current investment loss. If the invested entity realizes any net profits later, the investing enterprise shall, after the amount of its attributable share of profits offsets against its attributable share of the un-recognized losses, resume recognizing its attributable share of profits.

## ③purchase of minority equity

When preparing consolidated financial statements, the additional long-term equity investment for the purchase of minority equity, and the difference of attributable share of net asset for which the subsidiary owns and starts on a continuous measurement from the acquirement date (or the combination date) calculated according to the new proportion of shares shall be adjusted if the capital reserve is insufficient to dilute, the retained earnings shall be adjusted.

## ④the disposal of long-term equity investment

In the consolidated financial statements, under the circumstances that the parent company does not lose the control on the subsidiary company, the partial disposal of the long-term equity investment, the difference between the disposal amount and the net asset by the disposal of long-term equity investment shall be recorded into the ownership's equity. If the parent company loses the control on the subsidiary company for the disposal of its long-term equity investment, it shall be disposed according to the relevant accounting policies described in the Method for VII.1. Preparation of consolidated financial statements in this Notes

As for the disposal of the long-term equity investment under the other circumstances, when disposing of a long-term equity investment, the difference between its book value and the actual purchase price shall be included in the current profits and losses. If any change other than the net profits and losses of the invested entity occurs

and is included in the owner's equity, the portion previously included in the owner's equity shall, when expiring of a long-term equity investment measured by employing the equity method, be transferred to the current profits and losses according to a certain proportion. As for the remaining equity, it shall be recognized as the long-term equity investment or other relevant financial assets according to its book value and make subsequent measurement in the light of above-mentioned accounting policies of long-term equity investment or financial assets. If the remaining equity shall be measured from the cost method to the equity method, it shall be retrospectively adjusted in accordance with relevant stipulations.

(3) recognition basis to have to do joint control or have significant influences on the invested entity. The term "control" refers to the power to determine the financial and operating policies of an enterprise and obtain benefits from its operating activities of the enterprise.

The term "joint control" refers to the control over an economic activity in accordance with the contracts and agreements, which does not exist unless the investing parties of the economic activity with one an assent on sharing the control power over the relevant important financial and operating decisions.

The term "significant influences" refers to the power to participate in making decisions on the financial and operating policies of an enterprise, but not to control or do joint control together with other parties over the formulation of these policies.

When ascertaining whether or not it is able to control or have significant influences on an invested entity, an enterprise shall take into consideration the invested enterprises' current convertible corporate bonds and current executable warrants held by the investing enterprise and other parties, as well as other potential factors concerning the voting rights.

(4) impairment test method impairment provision method

The Bank shall, on each day of balance sheet, make a judgment on whether there is any sign of possible assets impairment for the long-term equity investment. Where any evidence shows that there is possible assets impairment, the recoverable amount of the assets shall be estimated. If the estimated recovery amount is below its book value, according to its difference, an impairment provision shall be made and be recorded into the current profits and losses.

Once any loss of asset impairment is recognized, it shall not be switched back in the future accounting periods.

11. Investment Real Estates

Investment real estates for the Bank includes the right to use any land which has already been rented, the right to use any land which is held and prepared for transfer after appreciation and the right to use any building which has already been rented.

The Bank makes the subsequent measurement to the investment real estate through the cost pattern. For the investment real estates applied to the subsequent measurement of through the cost pattern, the depreciation policy and amortization method are the same as the same or identical fixed assets and intangible assets.

The Bank shall, on the day of balance sheet, make a judgment on whether there is any sign of possible assets impairment for the investment real estates. If any sign for impairment occurs, the recoverable amount of the assets shall be estimated and the impairment test shall be made.

①The current market price of investment real estates falls, and its decrease is obviously higher than the expected drop over time or due to the normal use;

②The economic, technological or legal environment in which the enterprise operates, or the market where

the investment real estates is situated will have any significant change in the current period or in the near future, which will cause adverse impact on the enterprise;

③The market interest rate or any other market investment return rate has risen in the current period, and thus the discount rate of the enterprise for calculating the expected future cash flow of the investment real estates will be affected, which will result in great decline of the recoverable amount of the assets;

④ Any evidence shows that the investment real estates have become obsolete or have been damaged substantially;

⑤The investment real estates have been or will be left unused, or terminated for use, or disposed ahead of schedule;

⑥Any evidence in the internal report of the enterprise shows that the economic performance of the investment real estates have been or will be lower than the expected performance, for example, the net cash flow created by investment real estates or the operating profit (or loss) realized is lower (higher) than the excepted amount, etc.; And

⑦Other evidence indicates that the impairment of investment real estates has probably occurred.

The recoverable amount shall be determined in light of the higher one of the net amount of the fair value of the investment real estates minus the disposal expenses and the current value of the expected future cash flow of the assets. The Bank shall, on the basis of single item investment real estates, estimate the recoverable amount. Where it is difficult to do so, it shall determine the recoverable amount of the group assets on the basis of the investment real estates group to which the asset belongs. The recognition of an asset group shall base on whether the main cash inflow generated by the asset group is independent of those generated by other assets or other group assets.

If recoverable amount of the single item investment real estates and the investment real estates group is lower than its carrying value, the carrying value of the asset shall be recorded down to the recoverable amount, and the reduced amount shall be recognized as the loss of asset impairment and be recorded as the profit or loss for the current period. Simultaneously, a provision for the investment real estates impairment shall be made accordingly. Once any loss of asset impairment for the investment real estates is recognized, it shall not be switched back in the future accounting periods.

## 12. Fixed assets

Fixed assets refers to premises and buildings, mechanical equipment, electronic equipment, means of transport with a service life over one year that the Bank holds for operating purpose. Premises and buildings mainly include network, properties and office buildings of branch offices. Fixed assets shall be measured based on historical costs and listed in terms of net value after original value deducting grand total depreciations and impairment reserve. Historical costs include the direct expenditure on the acquirement of fixed assets.

Subsequent expense of fixed assets refers to costs of updating and repairing in the use process of the fixed assets. The settlement principle for subsequent expense is as follows: where fixed assets meet the recognition requirement, they shall be recorded into the cost, while deducting the book value of the replaced part; where fixed assets does not meet the recognition requirement, they shall be recorded into the current profits and losses.

Fixed assets are depreciated by means of composite life method and withdrawn within the estimated service life according to their credit value minus estimated net residual value. For fixed assets whose impairment reserve has been withdrawn, the amount of depreciation can be confirmed according to the book value after deducting

impairment reserve and the years available during future period.

Estimated service life, rate of net residual value and annual rate of depreciation of fixed assets are listed as follows:
