As the economic interest cannot be produced due to fixed assets being disposed or anticipated utilization or disposal, the confirmation of fixed asset shall be terminated. The sum of incomes from sale, assignment, scrapping of or disposal for damage in fixed assets deducting the net book value and relevant taxes and fees shall be charged to current gains and losses.

As the recoverable amount of fixed assets is lower than its book value, the book value shall be written down to the recoverable amount.

## 13. Works in process

The cost of works in process is recognized according to the actual construction expenses, including various construction expenses in process ad other relevant expenses. Works in process shall be carried as fixed assets when they are available for predicted use.

With regard to the impairment test method and impairment provision method of the works in process, see IV17. The impairment of non-current nonfinancial assets in this Notes for detail.

## 14. Settled assets

Settled assets means physical assets or property right that the Bank is obtained from debtors, guarantors or a third person for compensation due to the performance of creditor's right or security lien according to law.

Settled assets should be charged to account based on fair value from the date of obtaining them and the difference between fair value and book value of relevant assets and tax fee paid shall be charged to current gains and losses. There is no depreciation or amortization for settled assets.

Expenses occurred in the course of keeping assets for debt assets shall be directly charged to other operating cost, and expenses happened in the process of handling assets for Settled assets shall be offset deduction from the disposal income.

In principle, it is not allowed to lease settled assets obtained. In case the settled assets that surely fail to be disposed within the specified time subject to objective conditions, can be leased temporarily within the disposal time limit under the condition that the establishment of lease relationship does not influence the disposal of assets. Rental income is charged to other operating income.

The disposed earnings of settled assets shall be charged to non-operating income as they are acquired, and disposal loss shall be charged to non-operating income.

15. Pricing and amortization method of intangible assets

(1) Pricing method of intangible assets

### 锦州银行 Annual Report 2010 年度报告

Intangible assets include land use right, proprietary technology and non-proprietary technology and so on. Intangible assets brought in shall be used as actual costs in terms of the purchase price actually paid and other relevant expenditures.

For intangible assets invested by investors, actual costs should be defined according to the value stipulated in investment contract or agreement, but the actual costs should be determined in accordance with the fair value if the value stipulated in contract or agreement is not fair and equitable.

If the intangible assets obtained by the exchange of non-monetary assets are commercial in nature, they shall be charged to account according to the fair value of assets surrendered, or else, they shall be charged to account according to the book value of assets surrendered.

Intangible assets acquired through debt reorganizing shall be confirmed according to their fair value.

(2) Method and term of amortization of intangible assets

The land use right of the Bank shall be amortized on average according to the year limit of transfer from the date of transferring (acquiring the right of land use), proprietary technology non-proprietary technology and other intangible assets shall be amortized on average by installment in accordance with the shortest one among the three including estimated durable years, beneficial years specified in contract and valid years stipulated by law.

(3) Impairment test method and impairment provision method of intangible assets

With regard to the impairment test method and impairment provision method of intangible assets, see 17. The impairment of non-current nonfinancial assets in this Notes for detail.

## 16. Long-term expenses to be apportioned

The long-term expenses to be apportioned mean various expenses with a apportion term more than one year (exclusive one year) that has occurred but should be born by current period and different periods later. Long-term repaid and deferred expenses shall be charged to account according to actual expenditure and amortized on average within the beneficial period of a project.

The long-term expenses to be apportioned of the Bank are mainly the expenses on decoration of premises leased for operating.

## 17. Impairment of non-current nonfinancial assets

For the non—current nonfinancial assets including fixed assets, Works in process, intangible assets with limited useful life, investment real estates measured through the cost pattern, as well as the long-term equity investment on the subsidiary company, joint enterprise and associated entity, The Bank shall, on the day of balance sheet, make a judgment on whether there is any sign of possible assets impairment. If any sign for impairment occurs, the recoverable amount of the assets shall be estimated and the impairment test shall be made. For the intangible assets with limited useful life and the intangible assets not available for use, whether any sign occurs, the impairment test shall be made every year.

If the test result indicates that the estimated recovery amount is below its book value, according to its difference, an impairment provision shall be made and be recorded into impairment losses.

The recoverable amount shall be determined in light of the higher one of the net amount of the fair value of the assets minus the disposal expenses and the current value of the expected future cash flow of the assets. Assets impairment provision shall be measured and recognized on the basis of single item assets. Where it is difficult to do so, it shall determine the recoverable amount of the group assets on the basis of the assets group

to which the asset belongs. The term "group assets" refers to a minimum combination of assets by which the flow-in cash shall be independently generated.

Once any loss of asset impairment is recognized, it shall not be switched back to the restored value in the future accounting periods.

## 18. Remuneration of employees

The remuneration of employees chiefly includes expenditures related to the acquirement of services provided by employees, such as wages, bonus, allowance and subsidy, welfare expenses for employees, social insurance premium and public accumulation fund of housing, trade union funds and educational fund of employees, Non-monetary welfare, dismissing welfare, early retirement compensation, etc.

During the accounting period of an employee's providing services to an enterprise, the Bank shall recognize the compensation payable as liabilities.

The Bank take part in the Social Security System for employees organized by the government institution according to relevant stipulations including basic endowment insurance, Medical insurance, Housing accumulation fund and other social security system, the corresponding expenditure shall be recorded into relevant asset cost or the current profits and losses.

If an enterprise cancels the labor relationship with any employee prior to the expiration of the relevant labor contract or brings forward any compensation proposal for the purpose of encouraging the employee to accept a layoff, Where the enterprise has formulated a formal plan on the cancellation of labor relationship or has brought forward a proposal on voluntary layoff and will execute it soon, at the same time The enterprise is unable to unilaterally withdraw the plan on the cancellation of labor relationship or the layoff proposal, the enterprise shall recognize the expected liabilities incurred due to the compensation for the cancellation of the labor relationship with the employee, and shall simultaneously record them into the profit or loss for the current period.

## 19. Bonds payable

The bonds issued by the Bank, shall regard the actual issue value aggregate as the cost of book value. The difference between issue value aggregate and bond book value aggregate shall be amortized as premium or discount during the duration of the bonds.

## 20. Interest income and expenditure

Besides financial assets and liabilities being measured at their fair value and their changes being charged to current profit and losses, interest income and expenditures of other interest-bearing assets and liabilities shall be confirmed by means of effective interest method.

The effective interest method means a method calculating their amortized costs as well as interest income or interest expenses at various stages according to the effective interest of financial assets or liabilities (containing a group of financial assets or liabilities).

The effective interest refers to an interest rate that is used for discounting the future cash flow of financial assets or liabilities during anticipated survival period or during applicable shorter period into present book value of these financial assets or liabilities.

While defining effective interest, the Bank shall estimate future cash flow on the basis of taking into consideration all contract clauses of financial assets or liabilities (including right of paying up a loan ahead of schedule, rising tendency options and similar options and so on), but without consideration of future credit loss.

Various charges, transaction expenses and premium price or reduced value etc. paid or imposed between

parties signing a contract of financial assets or liabilities, and that attribute to the component of effective interest shall be taken into consideration while determining effective interest. When the future cash flow or survival period of financial assets or liabilities is unable to reliably estimated, it is necessary to adopt contract cash flow of these financial assets or liabilities within the entire contract period.

## 21. Fee and commission income

Fee and commission income shall usually be confirmed while offering relevant services.

Commission charges produced while engaging in bargaining of assets, or participating in the third party to conduct bargain transaction of assets (such as purchasing customers' loans, securities or selling them) shall be confirmed as the relevant transactions are accomplished.

## 22. Government subsidies

Government subsidy means the monetary or non-monetary assets obtained free by the Bank from the government, but excluding the capital invested by the government as the owner of the enterprise.

If a government subsidy is a monetary asset, it shall be measured in the light of the received or receivable amount. If a government subsidy is a non-monetary asset, it shall be measured at its fair value. If its fair value cannot be obtained in a reliable way, it shall be measured at its nominal amount. The government subsidies measured at their nominal amounts shall be directly included in the current profits and losses.

The government subsidies pertinent to assets shall be recognized as deferred income, equally distributed within the useful lives of the relevant assets, and included in the current profits and losses. As for the government subsidies pertinent to incomes, Those subsidies used for compensating the related future expenses or losses of the enterprise shall be recognized as deferred income and shall include in the current profits and losses during the period when the relevant expenses are recognized; or Those subsidies used for compensating the related expenses or losses incurred to the enterprise shall be directly included in the current profits and losses.

If it is necessary to refund any government subsidy which has been recognized, if there is the deferred income concerned, the book balance of the deferred income shall be offset against, but the excessive part shall be included in the current profits and losses; and if there is no deferred income concerned to the government subsidy, it shall be directly included in the current profits and losses.

## 23. Income tax and deferred income tax assets and liabilities

The income tax is the total of current income tax and deferred income tax.

The current income tax is the amount of current income tax calculated in terms of current taxable amount of income. The taxable amount of income derives from making corresponding adjustment to current accounting profit before tax in accordance with relevant stipulations in tax law.

Deferred income tax assets and liabilities are confirmed according to the calculation of difference (temporary difference) between tax-figuring basis of assets and liabilities and its book value. For offsetting deficit and offsetting deduction of taxation whose taxable amount of income can be offset deduction in subsequent years in accordance with the stipulations in tax law, they may be considered temporary discrepancy to confirm corresponding deferred income tax assets. For those temporary differences formed from initial affirmation of assets produced in the transaction of neither influencing accounting profit nor taxable amount of income (or may offset against deficit), no corresponding deferred income tax assets should be affirmed. For deferred income tax assets and deferred income tax liabilities at the statement of assets and liabilities day, they should be measured in accordance with and applicable rate of tax during the period of expectedly recovering this assets or paying off this liabilities.

The confirmation of deferred income tax assets is limited to the taxable amount of income that the Bank could possibly gain for offsetting against temporary difference, deficits that can be offset deduction and offsetting taxation.

Deferred income tax corresponding to the fair value of financial assets available for sale shall be charged to the shareholders' equity and then transferred into current gains and losses when relevant financial assets are sold.

## 24. Operating lease

The Bank regards the lease where the leaser retains the main risks and remuneration of leased assets as the operating lease. The operating lease of the Bank includes the operating places and devices that the parent bank and other branches have leased. A sum of money paid shall be charged to operating expenses by amortization by means of composite life method within the lease term.

When the lease agreement is terminated in advance, all penalty expenditure paid for leaser shall be charged to current gains and losses as the agreement is terminated.

## 25. Contingent liabilities and acceptance

The contingent liabilities refer to the potential obligations formed in the past transactions or matters and its existence must be proved through occurrence or none occurrence of the future undefined matters; or current obligations formed in the past transactions or matters. Performance of this obligation is not that economic interest may be caused to flow off businesses or the amount of money of this obligation cannot be reliably measured.

The contingent matters will be revealed only in the annotations of financial statement. Only when this matter probably causes economic interest to flow off and this amount of money can be reliably measured, this matter shall only be confirmed and withdrawn.

Acceptance means promise to pay made to the bills that the Bank had issued to the customers. The Bank held that most business of acceptance would be settled at the same time that customers made payment. Acceptance is to be accounted in the subjects outside financial statement, or to be revealed as contingent liabilities and promise.

## 26. Guarantee contract

The Bank shall draw up following guarantee contracts: Letter of credit and letter of guarantee. These guarantee contracts shall allow the Bank to pay a sum of money to the holder of guarantee contract on behalf of the guaranteed party in case the guaranteed party fails to perform contract terms.

The guaranteed amount of money of guarantee contract shall be shown as a subject outside financial statement.

## 27. Estimated liabilities

Owing to the current obligations formed from pending action, reorganization and deficit contract, its performance will probably cause outflow of economic interest. As the amount of money of this obligation can be reliably measured, it is confirmed as estimated liabilities. For operating deficit in the future, no estimated liabilities shall be confirmed.

The estimated liabilities shall be initially measured in accordance with optimum estimate of expenditure necessary for executing relevant current obligations and in overall consideration of risks, uncertainty and time value of money and other factors related to contingent matters. When the influence of time value of money is significant, the optimum estimates shall be determined by discounting relevant future cash outflow.

## 28. Commission businesses

Acting as an agent or going in for other commission businesses, the Bank holds and manages assets for

other institutions. This financial statement does not contain trusteeship assets and incomes derived from them that for them. The Bank, acting as a consignee, trustee and an agent, undertakes the obligation of keeping and makes promise to return to customers.

The Bank grants trust loans for third-party accommodators. As a middleman, the Bank grants loans to accommodator in accordance with the aspiration of the third party providing fund, and signs a contract with the third-party accommodator to agree on being responsible for managing and recovering loan by replacing the third party. The third-party accommodator shall decide by himself the requirements and clauses of entrusting loan, including purpose, amount of money, and interest rate of loan and arrangement of paying up a loan. The Bank shall impose commission charge of entrust loans and confirm it as income in terms of ratio during the period of providing services. The Bank does not undertake the risk of loss produced by a loan.

## 29. Other comprehensive income

Other comprehensive income refers to interest earned which is not recognized in gain and loss and the net amount which is including the deduction of income tax in accordance with the Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises

## 30. Segment reporting

The operation segment is divided in accordance with the internal organizational structure, Management requirements, Internal reporting systems, which is the basis of Reporting Segment.

The operating segment is divided into in accordance with the characteristics of the Bank's business corporation banking, personal banking, fund business and other business.

As one part of asset and liability management, the sources and application of the Bank's funds shall be allocated in various business segments. The internal transfer price of the capital is recognized according to the benchmark interest rate released by People's Bank of China as well as present market interest rate. The Bank makes the confirmation on the allocation of receipts and expenses of corporation banking, personal banking and fund business. The allocation method is to calculate the receipts and expenses of the internal capital transfer of corporation banking, personal banking and fund business by the way of the fluctuation of margin based on that year's deposit interest—payment rate as well as the average daily balance of private banking employed by corporation banking and fund business.

#### . important accounting estimation and judgment

Based on historical experience and such factors as reasonable expectation to the future events, the Bank has made the following indefinite estimation and would continue to carry out follow-up evaluation. The main domains of book value of assets and liabilities influenced by accounting estimation and hypothesis are listed as follows. It is unreal to define the influence brought by changes in the following important hypothesis or other estimations. The Bank will possibly make a major adjustment to these estimations in accordance with actual conditions in the days to come.

## 1. Loan asset impairment loss

Unless the known conditions indicated that value—decreasing loss have already taken place during the reporting period between the evaluations every time, the Bank will carry out periodical check to the book value of customers' loans and make judgment of whether or not there exists objective evidence showing that value—decreasing loss has occurred in customers' loans. If the objective evidence indicated that value—decreasing loss has occurred in customers' loan, the Bank will estimate the amount of value—decreasing loss. The amount of value—decreasing

loss is the difference between the book value of customers' loan and current value of estimated future cash flow. In the course of estimating value—decreasing loss, it is necessary to make a great number of judgment to define whether or not there exists objective evidence showing occurrence of value—decreasing loss, and require to make a major estimation to the current value of estimated future cash flow so as to reduce the discrepancy between estimated value—decreasing loss of loan and actual value—decreasing loss of loan.

## 2. Impairment loss of other assets

The Bank makes impairment evaluation per year to other assets with exception of customers' loans to judge whether or not there exists a hint of decrease in estimated cash flow. The Bank also estimates the amount of decrease in cash flow and makes depreciation of impairment reserve to it.

## 3. Fair value of financial instruments

For financial instruments unable to obtain quotations of active market, the Bank confirmed their fair value using assessment technique. Technique of assessment contains present discounted value (PDV) of cash flow and so on. Technique of assessment should as much as possible use observable data in actual operation, but management level is still required to make estimation to such factors as credit risk of parties conducting transactions, fluctuation ratio of market and its relativity. If change in the hypothesis of the above factors takes place, evaluation to the fair value of financial means will be affected.

## 4. Held-to-maturity investment

The Bank regards non-derivative financial assets with a fixed or definable paid amount and a fixed maturity date as a held-to-maturity investment. This classification involves major judgment. When related judgment is made, the Bank will take into consideration that whether or not it has willingness or ability by itself to hold this sort of investment up to the date due. If the Bank is about to sell at more than 5% of the total prior to selling relative to this investment before the investment is at maturity date, the Bank must reclassify the remainders of this sort of held-to-maturity investment into financial assets available for sale and measure the corresponding investment at their fair value, instead of amortized costs.

## 5. Income tax

Within the limit of taxable amount of income tax probably acquired for offsetting against and being capable of offsetting against temporary difference, the Bank will confirm deferred income tax assets produced from temporary difference that is offsetting against deduction. At the statement of assets and liabilities day, the Bank will make recheck to the book value of deferred income tax assets. If it is likely to fail to obtain adequate taxable amount of income for offsetting against deferred income tax assets during future period, the book value of deferred income tax assets should be decreased. Therefore, the Bank needs to make major judgment to the tax disposal of relevant transactions in accordance with relative tax laws and regulations, and make major estimation to the possibility of whether or not being able to obtain enough taxable amount of income for offsetting against deferred income tax assets.

## V. Description of principal accounting policies, changes in accounting estimation and major accounting errors

None.

### 49. Segment reporting

The major businesses of the Bank are commercial loan and acceptance of deposits, and the existing personal and corporate loan funds mainly derived from customers' deposits. The segment information is listed at the business segments of the Bank.

Business segment reports as the segment of the Bank. The Bank provides such financial services depending on three major business segments: corporate banking business, personal banking business, and fund business. The segment income, operating results, assets and capital expenditure listed in business segments include the items directly under various segments and related items distributable to various segments based on rational standards. As part of assets liability management, the sources and use of funds of the Bank are distributed to various business segments according to the natures of their businesses. The internal transfer price of funds shall be subject to the level of both benchmark interest rate and current market interest rate.

Corporate banking business — the Banking service provided for corporate customers, including home and foreign currency deposits, loans, products in connection with trade, as well as settlement, agency, commission, credit authentication and other services.

Personal banking business — the Banking service provided for personal customers, including home and foreign currency deposits, investment deposit products, trusteeship, debit cards, credit, and the management, settlement, agency and credit authentication of personal assets and other services.

fund business —that including the management of interest rate, money market transaction, self-employment bond investment and assets management.

Other businesses— other business of the Bank means other segments that can not be independently listed and reported or the businesses that can not be assigned according to rational references.

### 5. Pending actions

By the end of December 31, 2010, Bank of Jinzhou had 153 cases filed to the court which were not closed with a total of 23,856,780,000.00 Yuan concerning the cases. The bank all acted as the plaintiff in these lawsuits. For the relevant asset involving in these lawsuits, the bank withdrew appropriate depreciation reserves on the basis of considering the returnability.

## X. Events occurred after the balance sheet date

Reviewed by the 22nd session of the 2nd Board of directors held on Mar 2, 2011, the annual profit distribution for the year 2010 was approved as follows:

(1) The bank withdrew 84,232,448.74 Yuan of legal surplus, which is 10% of the annual net profit;

(2) According to Administrative Measures for the Withdrawal of Reserves for Bad Debts of Financial Enterprises (Cai Jin [2005] No.49), the bank withdrew the general reserve of 186,966,278.25 Yuan based on 1% of the risk assets.

(3) Cash dividends would not be distributed at present.

The profit distribution plan above is yet to be approved by the Shareholders General Meeting.

The people's bank of China decided on January 20, 2011 to raise 0.5% of the deposit reserve ratio of deposit-taking financial institutions to 17%.

The people's bank of China decided on February 24, 2011 to raise 0.5% of the deposit reserve ratio of the deposit-taking financial institutions to 17.5%.

There is no other events occurred after the balance sheet date.

## XI. Related parties and their transaction

##### (1) Related parties and related natural persons

When a party controls or exert great affect on the other or both parties jointly control or exert great affect on a third party, and both parties or more are simultaneously under control of or affected by a third party or more parties, the related party relationships are constituted. The term “control” means having the right to decide the financial and business policies of an enterprise. The term “jointly control” means to jointly control a certain economic activity as per agreement in the contract. The term “significant effect” means having the power to participate in decision-making of the financial and business policies of an enterprise, but having no power to control or jointly control together with any other party (parties) the formulation of these policies.

Principle for confirmation of related parties:

Where shareholders hold 5% or more of the Bank’s stocks and those hold 5% or above of the Bank’s stocks, which are jointly held by two or more shareholders, we call them the related parties of the Bank.

The Bank’s shareholding subsidiaries, jointly owned companies and affiliated companies constitute the related parties of the Bank.

Other enterprises that are directly or indirectly controlled and jointly controlled or can exert significant effect on the Bank’s business by the insider of the Bank or their immediate relatives.

The insider of the Bank or their family members having a close relationship with them refers to all related natural persons of the Bank

All the directors, supervisors, senior executives of the headquarters and branches as well as the personnel having the right of deciding or participating in the credit-granting or assets transfer constitute the insider of the Bank.

## XII. Other Important Issues

On December 13, 2010, the Bank, pursuant to the Reply on the Establishment of Bank of Jinzhou Beijing Branch (YJF [2010]594), was approved to establish Beijing Branch. By the end of the reporting period, the branch's preparation was under way.

On December 24, 2010, the Bank, pursuant to the Reply on the Establishment of Jinzhou Beizhen Yimin Rural Bank (LiaoYin Jian Fu  $ [2010] $ No.487), was approved to establish Jinzhou Beizhen Yimin Rural Bank Corp., Ltd. By the end of the reporting period, the branch's preparation was under way. The Bank shall contribute

25,930,000 Yuan to the said bank, accounting for 49.68% of its equity capital.

3. Notes to abnormal conditions on the major items of financial statements

A. Balance sheet items:

(1) Closing amount of Deposits with the PBOC was 12,749,383,505.62 Yuan, up 42.98% compared with opening amount, which was mainly resulted from the increase of deposits and the rising of legal reserves rate.

(2) Closing amount of Deposits in correspondent banks was 1,629,559,988.71 Yuan, up 80.54% compared with opening amount, which was mainly resulted from expanding investment channel and strengthening trade cooperation so as to expand its investment scale

(3) Closing amount of Due to banks was 1,808,332,800.00 Yuan with opening amount zero, which mainly because its market rate is comparatively higher than other investment products so as to expand its investment scale

## 锦州银行 Annual Report 2010 年度报告

(4) Closing amount of Assets purchased under resale agreements was 15,320,800,000.00 Yuan up 234.82% compared with opening amount, which mainly because the increase of deposits resulted in its increase in order to improve fund application rate and strengthen the management on the liquidity.

(5) Closing amount of Interest receivable was 221,111,813.35 Yuan up 139.32% compared with opening amount, which was mainly resulted from the increase of interest-bearing assets.

(6) Closing amount of Loans and advances was 40,001,916,128.71 Yuan, up 31.39% compared with opening amount, which was mainly resulted from the expansion of loans scale.
